notes: Open by saying this is the intervention architecture, not another diagnosis slide. Walk left to right: target precisely, deliver crop-system advice, improve realization, then protect gains. Expect the question on sequencing; answer that market linkage and resilience should be designed upfront, not added after productivity work.
title: Gujarat can translate farm strength into broader income gains when **4** interventions connect data, extension, market access, and resilience
subtitle: The model is not a linear subsidy stack; it is an operating system that targets the right farmer systems, changes field decisions, improves realization, and protects gains against water and climate shocks.

blocks.title: Data-led targeting raises program hit rates by matching support to Gujarat’s distinct farm systems
blocks.body: Evidence focus: district segmentation, crop-water economics, farm-size differentiation, and farmer lists that separate canal, groundwater, and micro-irrigation contexts before resources are deployed.

blocks.title: System-specific extension improves adoption because advice must fit crop, water source, and smallholder constraints
blocks.body: Evidence focus: package-of-practice delivery tailored to cotton, groundnut, wheat, horticulture, and dairy-linked households; scheduling that reflects irrigation access; and service models built for smaller farms facing tighter cash flow and lower realized margins.

blocks.title: Market-linked services convert production gains into income by fixing the realization bottlenecks after harvest
blocks.body: Evidence focus: aggregation, grading, storage, cold-chain access, buyer linkage, and processing routes aligned to commodity-specific breaks, so horticulture, cotton, groundnut, and dairy output move through stronger price and quality channels.

blocks.title: Resilience tools protect the upside where water stress and climate exposure threaten repeatable farmer gains
blocks.body: Evidence focus: micro-irrigation scale-up, water-smart crop choice, climate advisory, risk planning, and local response models concentrated in districts where rainfall volatility, groundwater pressure, and smallholder vulnerability are strongest.
